name: update-import-safely
title: Update import (safe)
description: Import an updated XER into an existing P6 project safely: inspect the file, dry run the update, report what it would change and what the XER lacks, then apply only on the user's explicit yes. Use when the user wants to import or load an XER update into a project.

args.name: xer_path
args.description: Full path of the XER file

args.name: project
args.description: Project ID as shown in P6 (the project to update)

template:
Update project {project} from the XER file {xer_path}, safely: inspect the file, dry run the update, report what it would change and what the XER lacks, then apply only after the user's explicit yes.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules, checks before applying and before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order. Call 2 is a dry run: it writes nothing and returns a confirmation_token that you
keep for yourself and never show.
1. ins = p6_inspect_xer(path="{xer_path}"): file facts, projects in the file, pre-flight errors, warnings and info, global items reused or created.
2. dry = p6_import_xer(path="{xer_path}", mode="update", project="{project}"): dry run of the update (nothing is written): data date, refusal, counts per table, rows missing from the XER.

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

For this skill:
- File paths are written exactly as returned.

After the report, wait for the user's answers to the two questions:
- No, or no explicit yes to question 1: nothing is applied; say so.
- Yes to question 2 (remove the missing relationships, assignments or both): run the dry run again with
  the same arguments plus remove_missing=["TASKPRED"], ["TASKRSRC"] or ["TASKPRED", "TASKRSRC"], write
  the report again from its result and ask question 1 again: the token belongs to the arguments of its
  own dry run.
- Explicit yes to question 1: call p6_import_xer again with exactly the arguments of the dry run the user
  approved, dry_run=false and that dry run's confirmation_token (and confirmation_text when the dry run
  asks for it). P6 must be closed. Never show the token.
- Then report the backup taken and stale_projects of the result, ask the user to open P6 and press F9,
  and suggest a weekly update review once the F9 is done.

files.text:
# Update import of {project} from {xer_path} (dry run)

Nothing was written: this is the dry run. The import is applied only after your explicit yes.

[if: would_refuse]
The import would be refused as it is:

[table: refuse]
[end if]

## The file

- Written by P6 {file_version} on {file_date}; {file_bytes} bytes; encoding {encoding}; end marker %E: {end_marker}; unreadable characters: {bad_chars}.
- Project imported from the file: {xer_project}.

[table: xer_projects]

Rows per table in the file:

[table: file_tables]

## Pre-flight

Errors (a confirmed import refuses them):

[table: pf_errors]

Warnings:

[table: pf_warnings]

Information:

[table: pf_info]

Global items of the file (matched by name in the database, else created):

[table: global_items]

## Data date

Database {dd_database}, XER {dd_xer}. XER older than the database: {dd_older}.

[if: dd_older]
The XER data date is older than the project's: the import is refused unless you confirm that this older file is the one to import.
[end if]

## What the update would change

[table: counts]

Warnings of the dry run:

[table: dry_warnings]

## Missing from the XER

- Activities of {project} not in the XER: {miss_acts}. An import never deletes activities: delete them in P6 if they are obsolete.
- Relationships not in the XER: {miss_links}, plus {miss_links_on} on missing activities (never removed).
- Assignments not in the XER: {miss_asg}, plus {miss_asg_on} on missing activities (never removed).

[if not: would_refuse]
## Your decision

1. Apply this update import to {project} (yes or no)?
2. When it is applied, remove the relationships and assignments of {project} that are missing from the XER (remove_missing)? Without it they are kept.
[end if]

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- p6_inspect_xer cannot read the file: repeat its message and stop.
- p6_inspect_xer returns no preflight because the file holds several projects: list the Project IDs of
  the file (the projects table), say "This file holds several projects: export the one to import alone
  from P6", and stop.
- p6_import_xer says the project is not found or is an EPS node: repeat its message and stop.
- ins.preflight.errors is not empty: write the report (the import would be refused), say "Fix these
  errors in the source schedule, export the XER again, then run this skill again", and stop: ask no
  question.
- dry.data_date.older is true: write the report and say "The XER data date is older than the project's:
  is this older file really the one to import?". Only on the user's explicit yes run the dry run again with
  allow_older_data_date=true, write the report again from its result and ask the two questions then.

## Cross-checks (each pair must be equal)

1. ins.preflight.project = dry.preflight.project (same project of the file).
2. ins.preflight.errors = dry.preflight.errors.
3. ins.preflight.warnings = dry.preflight.warnings.
4. ins.projects.0.data_date = dry.data_date.xer (same XER data date).

If a pair differs, the file changed between the calls: run both calls again once. If it still differs,
say which pair differs and do not apply anything.

## Before applying (only after the report)

- The user said yes to question 1 in their own words: a question, a "maybe" or a silence is not a yes.
- The apply call has exactly the arguments of the dry run the user approved (path, mode "update",
  project, and remove_missing or allow_older_data_date only when that dry run had them), dry_run=false and
  that dry run's confirmation_token. A change of arguments needs a new dry run and a new yes.
- The confirmation token is never shown to the user.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you.
- Each table keeps the items in the order returned and stops at its cap; the counts table comes from
  dry.counts, never from the file's rows per table.
- The refusal block is kept only when would_refuse is true, the older data date block only when
  dd_older is true, the questions only when would_refuse is false.
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names, file paths and number formats
  exactly as formatted.

# Fields of Update import (safe)

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. ins = p6_inspect_xer(path="{xer_path}"): file facts, projects in the file, pre-flight errors, warnings and info, global items reused or created.
2. dry = p6_import_xer(path="{xer_path}", mode="update", project="{project}"): dry run of the update (nothing is written): data date, refusal, counts per table, rows missing from the XER.

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.

## Arguments

- {xer_path}: Full path of the XER file, as given
- {project}: Project ID as shown in P6 (the project to update), as given

## Units

- count: a count

## Slots

| Slot | Field (call.path) | Unit | Format | None | Meaning |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| file_version | ins.header.1 |  | text | n/a | P6 version that wrote the file |
| file_date | ins.header.2 |  | date | n/a | export date in the file header |
| file_bytes | ins.bytes |  | n0 | n/a | file size in bytes |
| encoding | ins.encoding |  | text | n/a | text encoding read (utf-8, else cp1252) |
| end_marker | ins.has_end_marker |  | flag | n/a | the file ends with %E (not truncated) |
| bad_chars | ins.replacement_chars | count | int | n/a | characters not readable in that encoding |
| xer_project | ins.preflight.project |  | text | n/a | Project ID of the file's project that is imported |
| dd_database | dry.data_date.database |  | datetime | n/a | data date of the project in the database |
| dd_xer | dry.data_date.xer |  | datetime | n/a | data date of the XER project |
| dd_older | dry.data_date.older |  | flag | n/a | the XER data date is older than the database's |
| would_refuse | dry.would_refuse |  | flag | n/a | applying these arguments would be refused |
| miss_acts | dry.missing_from_xer.TASK.count | count | int | n/a | activities of the project not in the XER (never deleted) |
| miss_links | dry.missing_from_xer.TASKPRED.count | count | int | n/a | relationships of the project not in the XER (removable) |
| miss_links_on | dry.missing_from_xer.TASKPRED.on_missing_activities | count | int | n/a | relationships of missing activities (never removed) |
| miss_asg | dry.missing_from_xer.TASKRSRC.count | count | int | n/a | assignments of the project not in the XER (removable) |
| miss_asg_on | dry.missing_from_xer.TASKRSRC.on_missing_activities | count | int | n/a | assignments of missing activities (never removed) |

## Table xer_projects

Rows: ins.projects, in the order returned, at most 10 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 10 items, add the line: Only the first 10 projects are shown.
No rows: write 'No project in the file.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).
